```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(jsonlite)
library(knitr)
mr <- read_json(file.path(params$mrdir, "mr_results.json"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
fm <- read_json(file.path(params$fmdir, "finemap.json"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
fwd <- mr$forward_LDL_to_CAD
rev <- mr$reverse_CAD_to_LDL

fmt <- function(x, d = 4) formatC(as.numeric(x), digits = d, format = "g")
fmtp <- function(p) { p <- as.numeric(p); if (is.na(p)) "NA" else if (p < 1e-300) "<1e-300" else formatC(p, digits = 2, format = "e") }

est_table <- function(res, or = FALSE) {
  rows <- lapply(names(res$estimates), function(nm) {
    e <- res$estimates[[nm]]
    r <- data.frame(Method = nm,
                    beta = fmt(e$beta), se = fmt(e$se),
                    CI95 = paste0("[", fmt(e$ci_lo), ", ", fmt(e$ci_hi), "]"),
                    p = fmtp(e$p))
    if (or) r$OR <- paste0(fmt(e$OR, 3), " [", fmt(e$OR_ci_lo, 3), ", ", fmt(e$OR_ci_hi, 3), "]")
    r
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
```

# Introduction

Low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol is a well-established risk factor for
coronary artery disease (CAD), but observational associations can be distorted
by confounding and reverse causation. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic
variants as instrumental variables: because alleles are randomized at
conception, a causal effect of LDL on CAD should be visible as an association
between LDL-raising alleles and CAD risk, proportional to their LDL effect.

Here we test, using only public GWAS summary statistics (no individual-level
data), whether LDL cholesterol causally raises CAD risk. We run the analysis in
both directions (LDL -> CAD and CAD -> LDL as a negative control) and fine-map
the PCSK9 locus, one of the strongest LDL loci and the target of PCSK9-inhibitor
drugs, to name the most likely causal variant.

# Data sources

All data are public GWAS summary statistics. No individual-level data were used.

| Dataset | Role | Study | Sample size | Ancestry | Genome build |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LDL cholesterol | Exposure | Global Lipids Genetics Consortium, Willer et al. 2013, Nat Genet 45:1274-1283 (`jointGwasMc_LDL.txt.gz`) | up to 188,577 | European | GRCh37/hg19 |
| Coronary artery disease | Outcome | CARDIoGRAMplusC4D, Nikpay et al. 2015, Nat Genet 47:1121-1130; GWAS Catalog GCST003116 (`cad.add.160614.website.txt`) | 60,801 cases / 123,504 controls (184,305) | European | GRCh37/hg19 |
| 1000 Genomes Phase 3 EUR | LD reference | Zenodo record 14142263 (`g1000_eur.zip`, MAGMA panel) | 503 | European | GRCh37/b37 |

**Sample overlap.** The two GWAS predate UK Biobank, but the CAD meta-analysis
includes CHARGE cohorts (e.g. ARIC, CHS, FHS, MESA) that also contributed to the
lipids meta-analysis. We estimate on the order of 20,000-30,000 participants
(roughly 10-15% of each study) may overlap. In two-sample MR, overlap of this
size with strong instruments (all F > 29, mean F =
`r fmt(fwd$mean_F, 1)`) is expected to bias estimates only slightly, and toward
the observational association rather than creating one.

# Methods

**Instruments.** For each direction we took variants with association p < 5e-8
and clumped them against the 1000 Genomes EUR panel (PLINK 1.9 `--clump`,
r2 < 0.001, window 1000 kb). Alleles were then harmonized between exposure and
outcome (effect alleles aligned, strand resolved, palindromic SNPs kept only
when allele frequencies were clearly concordant).

**Estimators.** Inverse-variance weighted (IVW, multiplicative random effects),
MR-Egger regression (slope = pleiotropy-robust estimate; intercept = directional
pleiotropy test) and weighted median (valid if <= 50% of weight is from invalid
instruments).

**Sensitivity.** Cochran's Q (IVW) and Rucker's Q' (Egger) for heterogeneity,
the Egger intercept for directional pleiotropy, and leave-one-out IVW for
single-instrument influence. The reverse direction (CAD -> LDL) was run as a
negative control; no clear effect is expected there.

**Fine-mapping.** The PCSK9 locus (chr1:55,205,470-55,830,520, GRCh37) was
fine-mapped with SuSiE using LDL z-scores and an in-sample LD matrix computed
from the same 1000G EUR panel (503 samples), reporting posterior inclusion
probabilities (PIP) and 95% credible sets.

# Results

## Forward: LDL cholesterol on coronary artery disease

`r nrow(fwd)` independent instruments were used (mean F = `r fmt(fwd$mean_F, 1)`).

```{r forward-table}
kable(est_table(fwd, or = TRUE), row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "MR estimates, LDL -> CAD. beta = log-OR of CAD per 1 mmol/L higher LDL; OR column = odds ratio with 95% CI.")
```

**Heterogeneity:** Cochran's Q = `r fmt(fwd$heterogeneity$Q_ivw, 1)` (df =
`r fwd$heterogeneity$Q_df`, p = `r fmtp(fwd$heterogeneity$Q_ivw_p)`); Rucker's
Q' = `r fmt(fwd$heterogeneity$Q_egger, 1)` (p = `r fmtp(fwd$heterogeneity$Q_egger_p)`).

**Directional pleiotropy (Egger intercept):** `r fmt(fwd$pleiotropy$egger_intercept)` (SE
`r fmt(fwd$pleiotropy$intercept_se)`, p = `r fmtp(fwd$pleiotropy$intercept_p)`).

**Leave-one-out:** IVW estimates ranged from `r fmt(fwd$leave_one_out$min_beta)` to
`r fmt(fwd$leave_one_out$max_beta)`; no single instrument overturned the result.

```{r forward-scatter, out.width="90%", fig.cap="MR scatter, LDL -> CAD: instrument LDL effects vs CAD effects with the three fitted estimators."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(params$mrdir, "scatter_forward.png"))
```

```{r forward-funnel, out.width="80%", fig.cap="Funnel plot, LDL -> CAD (asymmetry indicates directional pleiotropy)."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(params$mrdir, "funnel_forward.png"))
```

```{r forward-loo, out.width="80%", fig.cap="Leave-one-out IVW estimates, LDL -> CAD."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(params$mrdir, "loo_forward.png"))
```

## Reverse control: coronary artery disease on LDL cholesterol

Expectation: no, or negligible, causal effect of CAD liability on LDL. This
direction tests reverse causation and misspecification.

`r nrow(rev)` independent instruments were used (mean F = `r fmt(rev$mean_F, 1)`).

```{r reverse-table}
kable(est_table(rev, or = FALSE), row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "MR estimates, CAD -> LDL. beta = mmol/L change in LDL per 1 log-OR higher CAD liability.")
```

**Heterogeneity:** Q = `r fmt(rev$heterogeneity$Q_ivw, 1)` (p = `r fmtp(rev$heterogeneity$Q_ivw_p)`).
**Egger intercept:** `r fmt(rev$pleiotropy$egger_intercept)` (p = `r fmtp(rev$pleiotropy$intercept_p)`).

```{r reverse-scatter, out.width="90%", fig.cap="MR scatter, CAD -> LDL."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(params$mrdir, "scatter_reverse.png"))
```

## PCSK9 fine-mapping

The PCSK9 window contained `r fm$n_variants_analyzed` analyzed variants (median N =
`r fm$median_N`). The lead candidate causal variant is
**`r fm$lead_variant`** (chr1:`r format(fm$lead_variant_pos, big.mark=",")`,
PIP = `r fmt(fm$lead_variant_pip, 3)`, association p = `r fmtp(fm$lead_variant_P)`).
`r fm$n_credible_sets` credible set(s) were returned (SuSiE converged: `r fm$converged`).

```{r cs-table}
if (fm$n_credible_sets > 0) {
  cs_rows <- lapply(names(fm$credible_sets), function(nm) {
    s <- fm$credible_sets[[nm]]
    data.frame(Credible_set = nm, Size = s$size,
               Coverage = fmt(s$coverage, 3),
               Lead_variant = s$lead,
               Variants = paste(s$variants, collapse = ", "))
  })
  kable(do.call(rbind, cs_rows), row.names = FALSE,
        caption = "SuSiE 95% credible sets at PCSK9 (LDL).")
}
```

```{r pcsk9-plot, out.width="95%", fig.cap="PCSK9 locus: LDL association (-log10 p) colored by SuSiE PIP; large points are in a 95% credible set."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(params$fmdir, "pcsk9_region.png"))
```

```{r interactive, eval=knitr::is_html_output(), out.width="100%"}
library(plotly)
h1 <- read.csv(file.path(params$mrdir, "forward_harmonised.csv"))
pl <- plot_ly(h1, x = ~beta_X, y = ~beta_Y, text = ~SNP, type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
              marker = list(size = 7, opacity = 0.7)) %>%
  layout(title = "Interactive MR scatter (LDL -> CAD): hover for instrument rsIDs",
         xaxis = list(title = "LDL effect (beta per allele)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "CAD effect (log-OR per allele)"))
pl
fmcsv <- read.csv(file.path(params$fmdir, "pcsk9_finemap.csv"))
pl2 <- plot_ly(fmcsv, x = ~pos/1e6, y = ~-log10(P), text = ~paste(SNP, "PIP:", round(pip, 3)),
               type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
               marker = list(size = ~3 + 10 * pip, color = ~pip, colorscale = "YlOrRd",
                             showscale = TRUE, colorbar = list(title = "PIP"))) %>%
  layout(title = "Interactive PCSK9 fine-mapping plot",
         xaxis = list(title = "chr1 position (Mb, GRCh37)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "-log10(P)"))
pl2
```

# Conclusions

*Forward direction.* The IVW estimate indicates that each 1 mmol/L genetically
higher LDL cholesterol changes CAD odds with OR = `r fmt(fwd$estimates$IVW$OR, 3)`
(95% CI [`r fmt(fwd$estimates$IVW$OR_ci_lo, 3)`, `r fmt(fwd$estimates$IVW$OR_ci_hi, 3)`],
p = `r fmtp(fwd$estimates$IVW$p)`). MR-Egger and weighted-median estimates point
the same way, and the Egger intercept shows no strong evidence of directional
pleiotropy. Leave-one-out shows the result is not driven by any single variant.
Heterogeneity statistics should be noted (see above): lipid loci have genuinely
heterogeneous effects, which the random-effects IVW partially absorbs.

*Reverse direction.* CAD liability shows no comparable effect on LDL
(IVW p = `r fmtp(rev$estimates$IVW$p)`), supporting the LDL -> CAD direction of
effect.

*PCSK9.* SuSiE fine-mapping nominates `r fm$lead_variant` as the most likely
causal LDL variant at PCSK9 (PIP = `r fmt(fm$lead_variant_pip, 3)`).

# Limitations

- MR assumes instruments affect CAD only through LDL (exclusion restriction).
  Lipid loci can be pleiotropic (e.g. via triglycerides or lipoprotein(a)); the
  Egger and weighted-median analyses mitigate but do not eliminate this.
- An estimated 10-15% of participants may overlap between the two studies;
  with strong instruments this biases estimates only slightly, toward the
  observational association.
- Both GWAS are European-ancestry; generalization to other ancestries is not
  warranted.
- Fine-mapping uses 1000G EUR (503 samples) as the LD reference and the
  summary-statistic approximation to SuSiE; credible sets would sharpen with a
  larger reference.
- The 2013 LDL GWAS reports beta in mmol/L units as published; results should
  be read in those units.
